'''Friedrich Wilhelm Franz Meyer''' (1856–1934) was a German [[mathematician]] and one of the main editors of the ''[[Klein's Encyclopedia of Mathematical Sciences|Encyclopädie der Mathematischen Wissenschaften]]''.

== Life and work ==
Meyer studied at [[Leipzig University]] and the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]]. In 1878, he was awarded a doctorate by Munich. He studied further in Berlin under [[Weierstrass]], [[Ernst Kummer|Kummer]] and [[Leopold Kronecker|Kronecker]]. In 1880, he got the ''venia legendi'' at the [[University of Tübingen]]. In 1888, he became a full professor at the Bergakademie of Clausthal (today [[Clausthal University of Technology]]). From October 1897 until October 1924, when he retired, he taught at the [[University of Königsberg]].{{sfn | Burau | 2008 | p=Dictionary of Scientific Biography}}

The wide research work of Meyer (more than 130 papers) is centred basically on [[geometry]] and, specifically, on [[invariant theory]].{{sfn | Parshall | 1990 | pp=13–15 }}

Notwithstanding he is mainly known for he was one of the main editors{{sfn | Gray | 2008 | p=116 }} of the ''[[Klein's Encyclopedia of Mathematical Sciences|Encyklopädie der mathematischen Wissenschaften]]'' published from 1898 to 1933 in 23 separate books. Meyer was directly in charge to edit the geometry volumes.{{sfn | de Siqueira | 2015 | p=36 }}
